title: feat(sim): the field column read from below - march_up and cut_downs (#637 E2b)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Part of #637 (step E2b; design in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637#issuecomment-6787218007, sections 2-3). Depends on E2a (the bake, `cut_downs`).

After a baked flip the field holds cuts on BOTH sides: the earlier setup's solids are monotone downward in the new frame, the next setup's monotone upward. The column's material is `[max(mesh floor, lower cut's top), min(mesh top, upper cut's bottom)]`. The top is `march` as today (its `refine` reads `cut_ups`). The floor needs the mirror: `march_up` from the world floor, a mirrored `refine` descending to the LOWEST material centre and reading `cut_downs` (the entry going down), the cell boundary otherwise, plus the mirrored sliver law (E1: a sliver with no centre read from the record of the cell above the mesh top).

Also: `refine`'s "cell boundary where the sign flipped" is exact only for a lattice-aligned plane; a flipped stock bottom is not aligned in general. Both marches should read an uncut plane from the column's shell crossing (cached, `shell_crossings`) instead - the view read-back already does, through `floor_at`.

Done means: `SdfField::column_span(x, y)` answers `Material { top, floor } | Empty | Unreadable` on a baked field with cuts from both sides, exact to the parity suite's tolerances; a pinning test: block, slot from the top, `turned` by a flip, slot from the new top, every column's span equals the column body's (`Body::carry` + `simulate`) to 1e-6; `floor_at` keeps its API. No shipped verdict changes.
